questions.prompt: Once background agents are refused writes into the installed plugin folders, may a background agent still update CTOC? Your standing order is that CTOC updates run in background agents across your profiles.

options.label: Yes, only by running the installed CTOC's own update script as one plain call (Recommended)
options.description: The hook allows `node <installed CTOC>/src/commands/update.js` when the script is the loaded plugin's own update script by real path, the way the menu call is recognised today; any other form, or a write into a plugins folder by any other route, is refused. Your other profiles' plugin folders stay outside this plan (listed as a neighbour). Read in src/commands/update.js: the script installs what is on GitHub main plus anything already planted in the local marketplace clone (untracked files survive its git reset, and the clone's git config decides the remote); the clone is refused to editing tools, and on the shell only by the mistake guard.
options.pros: Keeps your background update routine working; an agent cannot use an editing tool to put its own code on the update path.
options.cons: A shell route the mistake guard cannot read could still plant a file in the marketplace clone that the next update installs; the other profiles stay unprotected until you schedule them; how those profiles are updated today is unverified; if the sandbox already blocks the update from a background agent (believed, to verify), the exemption buys nothing; the switched-off menu rule must get the same exemption when it is turned back on.

options.label: No, every update runs from the main session, and the other profiles' plugin folders are protected too
options.description: Every background agent call that runs the update script or writes any profile's plugins folder is refused; the owner runs /ctoc:update or the marketplace update in the main session, one command per profile.
options.pros: No exemption to get wrong; covers your other profiles in the same plan.
options.cons: Ends the background update routine you asked for; updates show up in the foreground.

questions.prompt: Besides the installed plugin folders, four related places let an agent run code Claude Code loads: hooks in agent and skill frontmatter, the MCP server files (.mcp.json and the user-level .claude.json), and the file passed with --settings. Do they belong in this plan?

options.label: No, this plan covers the plugin folders; the four stay listed as neighbours for you to schedule (Recommended)
options.description: Each needs a different rule: agent and skill files are ordinary build targets in user projects, .claude.json is rewritten by Claude Code itself (believed), and the hook cannot see the --settings argument (believed). Keeping them apart keeps this increment small and its false refusals at zero for ordinary work.
options.pros: Small, reviewable increment that closes the measured gap first; no new false refusals on files agents edit in normal work.
options.cons: Code planted through those four places can still rewrite the plugin folder outside any tool call until they are scheduled.

options.label: Yes, cover all four in this plan
options.description: The plan grows to refuse background agents' writes to agent and skill frontmatter hooks, both MCP files and the --settings file, each with its own measurement.
options.pros: One plan closes every known route that runs code outside a tool call.
options.cons: A much larger change with real false-refusal costs in user projects and two open measurements before it can be built.
